page: Microsoft Azure D192ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 192 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 96 physical Intel Xeon 8573C cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor architecture is x86_64 and includes a 260 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is bundled, consisting of 11,339 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, though the instance does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results show top-tier multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 159,457.54 and a Passmark CPU score of 123,256.33. The hardware features Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which contribute to top-tier performance in extended instructions and cryptography. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 511.98 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 213.85 GB/sec for write operations. Single-core performance is moderate, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2,155.0, but multi-threaded operations like software compilation and ray tracing rank in the top tier.

Given its high resource density and massive local NVMe storage, the D192ds_v6 offers high qualitative cost efficiency for large-scale, I/O-intensive workloads that do not require GPU acceleration. The instance excels in database operations, achieving 211.88 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and top-tier Passmark database scores. It is highly suitable for enterprise database hosting, heavy multi-threaded software compilation, static web serving at scale, and medium-scale LLM prompt processing. However, the lack of a GPU limits its efficiency for large-scale LLM text generation.

It features 768.0 GB of RAM and a substantial 11,339 GB local NVMe SSD. While single-core performance is average, the instance delivers top-tier multi-core capabilities, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 159,457.54 and a Passmark CPU score of 123,256.33. It also demonstrates exceptional memory bandwidth and database performance, processing 211.88 million Redis SET operations per second. Lacking a GPU, this server is highly cost-efficient for non-accelerated, highly parallelized enterprise workloads. It is best suited for large-scale databases, heavy software compilation, high-throughput web serving, and multi-threaded data processing.
